paragraphs.text: A letter from Eusebius, patriarch of the Romans, to Papa, Catholicos of the East.

To my holy lord, Mar Papa the patriarch: Eusebius, your brother, bows before you. Just as the glory of God cannot be hidden, neither can the victories of his saints. The all-ruling, victorious Emperor Constantine, blessed forever, together with his mother, the faithful queen, rejoiced in your victories and marveled at your wonders. And just as they delighted, among the leading Romans, in the true reports of your godly conduct, may they also receive a blessing from your high priesthood, and from the holy throne of Mar Thomas the apostle, who [?] Addai the apostle, according to the tradition of the Church. They have made vessels for worship and sent them to you with their greetings in imperial letters. Receive them joyfully, my lord. Establish their commemoration within your church, and let it be an everlasting memorial. From the sea of your blessings, may blessings overflow upon them abundantly. And let prayer be offered without ceasing for us, for this city, and for our entire realm.
Another letter, from Judas Cyriacus, bishop of Jerusalem, to Papa. To Papias, Papa, chief of the priests and head

of the evangelists: Judas Cyriacus bows before your high priesthood in our Lord. Isaiah the prophet spoke beforehand about you and about saints like you, through whom the praise of the Lord is proclaimed from the ends of the earth,

among those who go down to the sea, among the inhabitants of the islands, and among the inhabitants of the wilderness. From the mountaintops let them cry out from their caves, and let those who dwell among the cliffs offer praise with the sound of their sacred songs. My lord, the many sufferings and dark afflictions in which you triumphed brought comfort and help to our holy city, through your endurance in all your struggles and the trials you suffered at the hands of the pagans. Both sorrow and joy took hold of us: sorrow because of our grief over

your high priesthood, and joy because you triumphed and received the crown of victory. You exalted the Church through your humiliation on its behalf. These very things were brought by many to the attention of Helena
the queen. And since she wishes to build up and exalt the Church of Christ in every region with every kind of adornment,

especially in the great cities, she wishes to build a church for the Lord Christ in your city, Seleucia. She asks permission from your fatherhood, and, along with permission, advice. As she instructed me, I have written to your high priesthood. But you, my lord, act according to the love of God that is in you, and tell her what will help her, so that she may be free from stumbling. Pray for us, and for the victorious king Constantine, her son, and for all who serve his kingdom.
[Letter] of Queen Helena to Papa.

To the chief priest of Christ and pure temple, the dwelling place of the Holy Spirit, my lord Mar Papa, Patriarch of the East: Your servant Helena offers homage at your holy feet with supplication. What shall I repay the Lord for all his benefits to me, that a sinful woman like me should openly write and send a letter and an imperial decree to saints and priests like you? I have learned, my lord, from David, the man of God's heart, who says: “I will praise the Lord
throughout my life, and sing to my God as long as I live.” I too, my lord, reflected within myself:

Since Christ has called us to all this greatness, and has given your son Constantine victory over all his enemies, through the power and help of the great sign of the cross, whose appearance from heaven overthrew the armies of the enemies, and the power of the holy Church has been exalted, I wish to magnify Christ's name myself in every place through the churches I build, through splendor and adornment with decorations of every kind, through the glorious ministry of the priests,

and through welcoming the needy. Now, my lord, what would it be helpful to undertake in your region, and in how many cities would it be appropriate to build? And is there anyone who would hinder this, or not? Let my sinful self be informed about these things by your letter, through the hand

of your son and holy disciple James, bishop of Nisibis. And pray for us, for your son King Constantine, and for his entire administration, that through your prayers it may prosper in every good and perfect work.
From Saint Papa to Queen Helena.

To the blessed mother, the faithful Queen Helena: Papa, servant of Jesus, worshiper and reverer of his cross. Peace. As for the things you asked of us, my lady the queen, our thoughts are insufficient to grasp what would be helpful and write to you. For the Christians of our region take pride in poverty, in imprisonment, and in afflictions of every kind. A small hut is spacious enough for our house of prayer. This is not because we are lazy or shrink from building, but so that large buildings do not bring the pagans' envy upon us, and Christian instruction is not diminished through the danger of the persecutions they stir up against us. Even the liturgical equipment you sent us causes us anxiety in keeping it safe. We are afraid to bring it out openly and use it in worship, lest it be taken from us on some pretext. We are afraid not only of the pagans, but also of the Jews and the Marcionites.
For since they were suppressed in your territory

by the authority of your kingdom, they fled from your decree and came to this region of ours. Their hatred increased, and they hated us with complete hatred. They are constantly fabricating accusations against us.

lies. And they become our accusers in secular courts. We write to tell you about our circumstances, like a sick person who shows his pain and illness to a physician. When a wise physician examines him, if there is hope for him, he knows how to treat him. The matters under our authority in our regions we have briefly set down

for Your Majesty. And the authority, wisdom, strength, might, and victory of Christ are with you. You should examine these matters with your knowledge and understand them through your authority. Tell us in our exile whatever you know will help. My lady, we have received the goodwill of Your Majesty as a gift greater than the building of the church. And because of you we also praise God, the Lord Christ. With supplication and entreaty, with love and reverence, from the heart's [?], we offer prayer for you in the church of God. And especially I, Papa, weak and sinful and the least of all
Christ's disciples, implore the Lord with sorrowful tears to appoint his right hand over you. May he command his holy angels to guard you in all your ways. And like a shepherd who carries his lambs
and his sheep on his shoulders, so may you carry the children of the church on the shoulders of your authority.
May all the faithful be strengthened by the stability of your reign, and through you may all be made strong,

the Christians who inhabit the world. I, Papa, have sent a greeting to Your Faithful Majesty in my own handwriting. May the cross of Christ our Savior, through which your reign has been raised up and exalted, guard the whole church under heaven. Amen.
A letter of Saint Jacob the bishop to Papa.
To our holy father, our teacher in the law, and the one who has brought us up in Christ:

the illustrious priest and honored elder, my lord, Mar Papa the patriarch: Jacob, your servant and the least of the disciples you have brought up, sends greetings in our Lord. My lord, the outrageous new deeds committed against Your High Priesthood by the servants of the enemy of our race— when news of them reached us through letters from our brothers and sons, the faithful, upright, and steadfast clergy who are with you, when the letters were read, anguish seized us, great astonishment fell upon us, and sorrow and distress ruled over us, and over the teacher Mar Ephrem, who has become renowned as a prophet within the church of God; especially the women,
the faithful women who receive help

for their sufferings from Your Fatherhood; and the young women who, together with their brothers, were afflicted by the adversary, who was rebuked through you; and the barren women who became fruitful through your prayers and blessings and saw lovely fruit from their wombs; and other men and women who listened to your spiritual conversation and received help from you, and time

after time had their requests answered through you—they could not endure or bear the terrible blows they suffered from the reading of the letters. The mourning and wailing in your city became more intense than that which arose over Josiah, king of Judah. And they filled our whole assembly with bitterness through the sound of their laments, saying, “Refuge of our prayer and great harbor of our blessing! Who has silenced your voice and hushed your songs? Who has withered your blessing right hand, so that we can no longer receive the sign of the cross from it, and it no longer hovers over us as you used to do? Who has cut off our paths to you and the course of our journey, so that we can no longer make our way to you? Where shall we go, our blessed father, in times of distress? At whose door shall we knock? For our generation has been stripped of holy fathers like you.” At these cries from the sons and daughters of Your Fatherhood, minds and bodies alike grew weak. Anguish seized the hearts of many, and tears streamed from people’s eyes like a spring of water.
And we implore that this suffering may soon pass from our city, and that our mourning and our house of weeping may receive comfort through the holy letters that you

send to us. But as for those sinful priests who sinned and caused innocent people to sin along with them— those belonging to the company of Aqballaha, Miles, and Habib, and their companions, who are your disciples— you know their innocence and acknowledge their complete simplicity. In their letters they earnestly pleaded that we should appeal to Your Holiness on their behalf, so that, if you command, [?] may be forgiven them, because they are without malice. And just as you forgave Mar
Simeon, forgive them too.

You consecrated them for the covenant and admitted them to the priesthood. Through the prayer and blessing they received from you, instruction was carried out through their hands. And because they had come from the world and possessed a simplicity consistent with their upbringing, they were unwittingly led into that by those wicked men who trouble the church. May the insult to Your Fatherhood and the turmoil that entered the whole church quickly recoil upon their heads, and may terrible wrath be fully carried out upon them through the retribution of justice. My lord, we have set down everything—what they did, how you yourself, Your Fatherhood, stretched out your hand toward the Gospel, and the trial that came at that very moment

upon Your Fatherhood. We wrote everything clearly and sent it to our holy fathers through the sons of your petition and the disciples whom you brought up. They had presented us with a request that our letters should be delivered through their hands. After them, we wrote and sent letters on two further occasions. They will soon reach you with our fathers’ letters. My lord, we and the whole church with us bear your sorrow and share in your trial, brought about through the activity of false disciples. Because you could not endure the injustice, oppression, and wickedness that from their mouths they were spewing out before the Gospel, you were overcome by anger, and as
a rash man you appeared. Yet this discipline, mercifully given to you by your Lord, has not harmed you.
And if

it seems good to you—as for those belonging to the company of Miles, Aqballaha, and Habib, together with their brothers—if I have found mercy in your eyes, my lord, regard these men as you would those who put deadly poison for you in the cup of the Eucharist. And with those who gave false testimony against you when you were stretched out for scourging before pagan judges. Because of their testimony, your sufferings, afflictions, scrapings, and lashes increased. Yet in the end you forgave them, and the rank of bishop
you bestowed on them. Let these too be counted like them,
and let them be forgiven. And also for my lowly self and for
our city and our country, which take refuge in your prayers, may you always remember us in your prayers.
Again, by Mar Ephrem the Teacher, to Mar Papa, Catholicos and Patriarch.

To the great and distinguished man of God, chosen among the ranks of the fathers, eminent in everything belonging to our Lord: my master, Mar Papa the Catholicos. Ephrem, a sinner, weak and the least of your disciples, through you offers you homage from afar, as though nearby before your holy feet. My lord, I am not unaware of myself: I know what I am and to whom I am writing a letter. Scripture too has taught me and said to me, “Do not seek things greater than yourself.” My lord, I have recognized, and continue to recognize, my littleness and your greatness in God. But because you, like compassionate fathers, have repeatedly taken the initiative and considered us in your letters worthy to be numbered among your disciples, I too, in this brief time, in this time full of deceit and losses, in this war

that has pressed upon the Church of God, and amid the losses inflicted upon your fatherhood by bands of betrayers, have longed to share with you through the small contribution of my words. My lord, Satan saw that your fatherhood had proved victorious in all the sufferings of virtue and in all the afflictions endured with patience. You entered the arena and proved victorious in your contest before the rulers of this passing world. You defied severe

sufferings and scorned bitter afflictions. The pagans were astonished, and their leaders marveled. With the spoils of your victories, you wove and gave the holy Church a great crown of your triumphs. And since Satan could not overcome your courage in the battle he arrayed against you through those who worship the elements and serve creation, he chose workers for himself from the false disciples who had been brought up within the Church. And because your fatherly rod was stretched out over them to discipline them
with compassion, so that they would not become weeds among the wheat in the Church’s field, nor be found to be rejected silver on the trading table
of the kingdom, instead of the good things you had done for them, for which they ought to have repaid you with good returns, like children toward their fathers, they repaid you evil for good

and hatred for love. They made their mouths like a catapult, their lips like a bow, and their tongues like a double-edged sword. They conceived injustice by night and gave birth to wickedness by day. They whispered in secret and formed a conspiracy in the darkness. They gathered others like themselves and formed bands of deceit for themselves. They also led astray others who have a reputation for virtue and who draw people after them in the name of virtue. When these ally themselves with them, their faction grows stronger and their wrongdoing gains credibility. And their oppression is accepted. Through these and similar deeds, Satan hoped to stain the victories of Your Fatherhood. When they prepared for battle, they presented themselves as zealous men. They drew their bows and shot falsehood like arrows, and deceit like a sword. And insults and abuse like stinking mud, and wrongdoing and oppression far more repulsive than [?]. Satan silenced those considered virtuous, so that they would not become advocates for the truth. He cast his covering over them and concealed in his murky darkness everyone’s understanding, knowledge, and thoughts, so that you would be left alone, with no one beside you in the battle that members of your own household
arrayed against you. He filled them with

anger and fury and inflamed them with groundless hatred against you. They struggle together and [?], raising their voices like people driven by force. They grind their teeth and bite their lips. They hunger for your holy flesh and thirst for your innocent blood. They have forgotten your good qualities, which really exist and are visible to everyone, while evil qualities that do not exist
in you
they all proclaim together. They all say, “We have heard,” speaking from hearsay. But an eyewitness [who had seen

what they were saying] is not found among them. Then, when he saw that his purpose had not been accomplished through all these things, he roused you as a zealous man and inflamed you as a believer, so that the wrongs done to you

and the injuries you suffered at their hands you would seek to redress through the holy Gospel. You stepped forward contrary to custom and acted contrary to proper order. You received a punishment that is entirely a crown of glory for you. [?] in this battle, so that you would not also be deprived of the sufferings for which a reward and recompense are reserved [for you]. My lord, if in your youth, with Christ’s help, you subdued the passions, crushed desires, and performed astonishing mighty deeds, and worked signs and wonders that no one in these generations has been seen to perform, and East and West agreed to your election as patriarch, and for sixty-

eight years you administered your stewardship with a good reputation—and now you have reached deep old age, having exercised the high priesthood of the patriarchate in East and West for sixty-eight years— there is no one in the priestly order who equals you, not even in a single one of these gifts you have received from your Lord. These things that have been said about Your Fatherhood at this time—if they can readily be said about the dead in their graves, then also about you. For not only have you descended into deep old age, beyond a hundred years, but even if you were a young man, with these scars and marks that you bear on every part of your body, and because of the combs, lashes, sufferings, afflictions, and pains, and illnesses through which you were worn down throughout all your various struggles—and especially now, when everyone knows that your body has grown cold and all

your limbs have become slack, and your desire for food and sleep has left you, and all your movements and senses have ceased to perform any of their functions— who has abandoned hope in both worlds so completely that he would contemplate saying these and similar things? And if those who are among the people who have hired themselves out

to work for Satan their father employ these and similar things because they belong to them, who among the children of the Church believes them of Your Fatherhood? And he listens to their insolent and destructive words, and is persuaded to be led astray and to accept what they say.

Unless perhaps he too is a servant of Satan like them. My lord, I have written these things to Your Holiness because I cannot understand against whom Satan has prepared this battle. For I see that, as regards your fatherhood, your administration, your throne, and the harm done to your body, they could not undo your great labors and your glorious conduct. And the writings produced by those insolent men, the sons of destruction, who called themselves shepherds of sin, could not remove you from the ministry of the high priesthood. Rather, they themselves have been brought low and cast down from their lofty ranks by the sentence you pronounced against them, especially Aqballaha and Miles and their companions. For from the time you issued a sentence against them, they became despised and outcast, and the teaching that had been raging in their hands has now been stopped. And Satan obtained what he wanted: that human beings should become estranged from eternal life. And again, along with

the earlier persecutions by the pagans that he raised against the church, there are also divisions and disturbances, turmoil, upheaval, and discord that have come upon the Christians. The whole church has been thrown into confusion, and this battle has grown greater and fiercer than the one waged by outsiders. For the emissaries of those wicked and insolent men are hurrying about, and their messengers are swift, carrying these writings that were composed against your fatherhood and taking them to various places. Although they cannot inflict any loss on your fatherhood, they are attacking the children
of the church through their stumbling blocks, their words, and their writings. And, as we have heard, many have fallen away from their hope. And through

disturbances, reports, and disgraceful writings of every kind, which they carry about and read aloud before them, as though for the joy and amusement of those insolent men themselves, and to cause many to stumble and lose heart. This battle has become like a tangled maze. For whether one looks toward your fatherhood,
or toward Aqballaha and Miles and their circle, or toward those insolent men, or
toward the whole church—every
place one looks, there one finds the full fury of the battle.

Your knowledge is sufficient to heal these things. Aqballaha and Miles and their companions weep and lament over themselves, and are remorseful and distressed. They appeal in writing to everyone who is a true friend of yours, asking him to intercede for them. They have also written to my wretched self, asking whether they might be regarded like Mari and John. Those men, when your fatherhood was being dragged in chains and fetters before the judges’ tribunal, were bitterly throwing stones at your fatherhood. They even dared to tear your clothes in the streets. They also pulled out the hair of your head and beard and spat in your face repeatedly before pagans and Jews. And after there was a little calm, and you were delivered from your bonds, you brought them close to you, reassured them, comforted them, and redeemed them. In your great humility you had mercy on them, and because of your overflowing love for them, your soul felt regret. Show this not only before Christians, but also before pagans and Jews, if it pleases your good will: just as until now you have repaid many people with good for evil, grant these people forgiveness too, as is your custom. And let there also be given to me, the least,

a little crumb from the table of your tongue. Among the lines of your writings, let there be a remembrance of my lowliness. Through your blessings upon me, let my poverty be enriched from your great treasury that never runs out. And let permission be given me by you. Please hear

my plea, and withdraw the prohibition you have imposed on me, so that the history I began to write about you I may complete, so that through you I may be remembered in the church of God, and the generations coming after us may know the great wealth of your glorious conduct, and the waves, surges, and storms that have swept over you time after time, and how you proved vigorous and watchful amid them. Your wisdom and knowledge have surpassed all the spiritual helmsmen of these generations. And may our city and our country, which mourn for your fatherhood, be comforted by your writings. Let a letter concerning public affairs also be written by your fatherhood to the fathers who are the true shepherds of the western territory, who are persecuted by the lawless followers of Arius. For they too are preparing to send their letters shortly to your fatherhood, through your servants and disciples, the clergy of the church of our city. Our holy father Mar Jacob, our bishop, and his entire flock, together with me in my misery and weakness, bow before you and ask for your prayers in our Lord, who preserves you at the head of his holy church.
A letter written by Mar Papa to the people of Nisibis.

The holy [?], together with the shepherds, teachers, priests, and all the ranks of faithful men and women, along with the children, young men, and virgins. Papa, weak as he is, chief of the bishops of the East: abundant peace in Jesus Christ, the guardian of his church. My beloved, I have not served human beings from my youth, so that I should receive a reward from human beings through praise spoken or written. Nor am I equal to the greatness of the rank to which I have been called. Rather, in every respect I am more deficient than anyone else. And now it is time for me to say, like the prophet Elijah, “Take my life from me, because I am no better than my fathers.” If Elijah, with all his mighty deeds, said that he was not as good as his fathers, how can I, who have been unable to reach even the smallest measure of my fathers,
compete with their greatness and strength? If I ran toward the dust of their feet and did not reach it, why am I running toward the mountain of their conduct,
especially at this time, when the surges rise up, the waves tower high, and fierce

storms and harsh battles are soon to come upon the church of God? And I, besides being unskilled in speech and deficient in knowledge, have also been disfigured by sins, by [?] and illnesses. I have been brought low by the many trials that have come upon me. Old age too has broken and humbled me, and especially the onslaught of trials that have swept over me from those

secret pagans who hide within the church and are called pillars and foundations by an empty title. And now they are destroyers and uprooters, yet they present themselves to people as builders and architects. And these things are still only the beginning of the birth pangs that are to come. Why do I need to live, when our disciples are our enemies, and our sons our accusers and judges? Because they are not true sons, no love was found in them
for God. Previously, however, when that struggle arose against me at the hands of those whose gods were more numerous than their towns,
and many Christians lost heart and denied Christ, they seized my humble self and bound me in harsh

fetters. They tortured me with hunger and thirst, with scourging and blows. Yet none of the sufferings I endured compared with the pain of the needles and hooks they placed beneath the nails of my hands and feet. And even when they pierced my hands and feet and passed cords through the holes in my body, and suspended me in the midst of the assembly of judges, stripped me, exposed me naked, and paraded me through the marketplace, Christ helped me in my weakness. He visited me in the intensity of my pain, gave me relief amid my many afflictions, and comforted me in the bitterness of my sufferings. In all these things I did not suffer as I have from this pain,
caused by these hidden pagans

and open enemies, who have corruptly and indiscriminately called themselves bishops: some of them through the written instructions of the deceased man who had been a bishop, who had occupied the throne without the laying on of hands
and called himself a bishop; some ordained by a single bishop each; and others claiming, “We have been ordained,” although, when their case was examined, they were found not to have been ordained.

Others had been ordained according to the canons, but when the bishops of prominent cities died, they moved from their own thrones and became adulterers through an impure partnership in a spiritual marriage. By this they defiled the whole body of the holy church. Others, with the assistance of insolent men like themselves, drove all the bishops from their thrones and occupied their places themselves. They killed and took possession within the church. Others were accused of acts alien to their calling, and others, because of the women living with them, with whom they behaved licentiously, practiced abortion and the destruction of infants. Others sold the property of churches and monasteries and enriched their relatives with it. Others, who present themselves as renunciants and ascetics, were found drinking wine, wearing garlands and singing, where it was not fitting. They were found committing sin upon sin, for most of them, in their laxity, turned aside together and became corrupt. While we wished to win them over privately as sons through admonition

from us and through the repentance they showed, they acquired the shamelessness of a brazen prostitute, and even surpassed her. And so that they might be without a head, without a judge, and without accountability, and fulfill their filthy desires without fear or dread, they all broke away together. This is the kind of profit they have made for the church of God! And now we have become a disgrace and a laughingstock, and pagans and Jews laugh at us and mock us.
Together. And now, do not concern yourselves with my affairs. For I, Papa, owe no one anything; rather, all that I owe, I owe to God alone. And knowing that I have nothing with which to repay
him, he has forgiven my debts in his mercy. For against him alone have I sinned. And it is better for me to be judged by the one to whom I am indebted than

to be judged by those to whom I owe nothing. They themselves are indebted to me, and every day they insult me. And you, our brother Mar Jacob, shepherd and leader of Nisibis, who requested writings of consolation from us: I have been commanded to tell you to put

comforts away from you, prepare yourself to face suffering, and ready yourself for afflictions. More than a helmsman at the rudder of his ship, be alert, keep watch, and remain vigilant in prayer over the afflictions of your city, the destruction of your congregation, the plundering of your church, and the stripping naked of the daughters of your people. Do not lose heart before the oppressor who comes against you like a river in flood, for the Spirit of the Lord will humble him. Instead, fasten your belt and stand courageously. Repair the breach in your people, and inform your fathers in the West that this persecution by the followers of Arius will soon cease. After a time, another great persecution will arise in your city. Persecution will come upon the flocks and their shepherds together. There will be an uprooting of the church, an overthrowing of altars, and mockery and outrage directed against the Scriptures and the holy mysteries. Nevertheless, the shedding of human blood will not be practiced. And when there is peace in the church of the West, there will be a great conflict in the church

in the East. There will be affliction and persecution the like of which has neither been written about nor heard of. The earth will be drenched with the blood of the saints. Wild animals will eat their corpses, have their fill, and grow fat.
And as for the holy men, our beloved sons Aqballaha and Miles, before your letters arrived,
we received them and admitted them to communion with us in the mysteries. We gave them authority to minister in their ranks as before, because

they are bridegrooms of blood to the holy church. Nevertheless, they are not being afflicted in their struggles as my beloved son Mar Simeon is, nor as Abduma, the elder and venerable man. The affliction in the church of the East will last a long time: four weeks of years. And three
patriarchs, one after another, like commanders of armies at the head of their troops, will be handed over to

terrible deaths. And you, the teacher Mar Ephrem, who have become renowned as a prophet in the holy church, and have asked us for authorization concerning the prohibition on your writing [?] histories about us, who are dead in our sins: neither you nor anyone else shall have authority to compose writings about us. Nor, moreover, those writings which those engaged in ministry and the scribes produced in their volumes and sent to the regions— [the leaders of the regions are not authorized], when they find in their churches and monasteries those writings which were written by impudent men to mock and insult me, to mutilate them, burn them, or erase them. Nor are they to make any correction in them supposedly for my edification. Rather, they are to be preserved just as they are, wherever

they are found, until the end of days. And our Lord himself, in his righteousness, according to the knowledge of his divinity, will demand justice for his holy church on that great day of judgment. And you, our beloved son, Mar Ephrem, tell the daughters of Zobah, especially those brought up under our instruction: Leave off mourning and lamenting over me, Papa. Think and reflect on the lamentation awaiting you and your city. Let them begin composing songs of lamentation. Let each woman teach her companion a sorrowful song. Let them begin learning and teaching one another. And warn them: Do not pamper your hair, which is destined to be shorn, with washing and hot baths. And your bodies, which are destined for mourning

and dancing, for sitting on the ground and spending nights on rooftops—do not pamper them beforehand. You too, go out in search of [?]. Prepare various songs and melodies of every kind, and rouse yourself. Gather your thoughts and prepare a quiet place for yourself, along with work and scribes

and many tablets for texts. For the labor will be hard for you: four weeks of years and two portions of the fifth week. Write and set down a record of all the evils coming upon the world: famines and pestilences, wars against the church, wars between kingdoms, and the plundering and pillaging
of one

by another; earthquakes and tremors in great cities; the absence of rain; and locusts that will take hold of the districts for ten years. I, Papa, have recorded these things in this letter as I was commanded. You have learned about the other things not recorded in the letter from our beloved and holy son, Mar Simeon. We have authorized him to assume the administration of the patriarchate after us. We have given him instructions about everything and warned him about the things we were allowed to know. We too made them known to him, Mar Simeon, in the presence of Mar Abduma, the priest and steward. And I am going to the grave, bearing sorrow upon my sorrows and sickness upon my sicknesses, like a father who sees his household uprooted and ruined, and the destruction

of his sons, his daughters, and all his people. I wrote all these things when they were still a week of years away. At the beginning of the second week, they will arise one after another, not all at once. Read the letter, and let nothing be written after it. Whoever dares to do so shall be excluded from the inheritance that Christ has prepared for his worshipers in the kingdom of heaven. May the whole church of your region be preserved through Christ’s help and through the prayers of those who fulfill his will. Our Lord be with us and with you and with the whole holy church. Amen.

[Again,] a synodical letter written by the Western fathers to Mar Papa, the Catholicos [and Patriarch], containing the annulment of the actions taken against him by the party of Miles and their companions.

To our excellent brother and fellow minister, abounding in victories, a second Elijah in the fervor of his zeal in Christ, Mar Papa, Patriarch and Metropolitan … Gaius, Peter, Paul, Clovianus, Cleon, Philip, Alexander, Eusebius, and Gregory, [and Magnus
and Gaddius and Gregory], and Armenites and Basilicus, together with all the rest of our brother bishops who are with us in the ecclesiastical assembly: in Jesus Christ, our Lord and Savior, peace
[be multiplied

to you. With] one mind we have written a letter to Your Holiness, my lord, because, when we were assembled, we hoped that through our agreement with one another we might, through shared counsel, find deliverance for the church of God among us, since it had not escaped the storms and waves of paganism: For before the ship had even reached the harbor, the storms of Arius’s followers broke upon us. Like ravenous wolves, they attacked Christ’s flock. While we were mourning these things, sighing and weeping, we anxiously considered by what means of prayer and supplication we might preserve the church in the truth of its faith. And while we had still found no consolation for this grief, another grievous blow was added to our severe and bitter wound, through the reading of two letters sent to us by our holy brother Mar Jacob, bishop of Nisibis, and by the holy Mar Ephrem the Syrian, who appeared like a prophet in our generation. When their letters had been translated from Syriac into Greek and read in the assembly, we learned from them about the outrage committed by shameless deceivers, with the consent of consecrated men who had received the title of bishop from you. These men, childish in knowledge and strangers to the understanding gained through toil and study, under the pretext of virtue

imagined that they had authority to do anything. They gave their support to those stunted and insolent men who had been removed and expelled by your holiness for that [reason], and to others who had been restrained by a prohibition against exercising the ministry of their ranks. They formed a band like savage wolves and sought to destroy the persecuted church in the East, through the working of their father Satan. They planned first to lay hands on the greatest and chief of the shepherds. They were not restrained by your many labors or by your advanced old age, or by the length and duration of your leadership over them. For you have exercised the administration of your high stewardship for sixty-eight years within
the church of God, and your high priesthood has shone upon East and West alike. Nor did they tremble or stand in fear of

God’s righteous judgment—those insolent men who, before the altar and the Gospel, would serve, some as accusers and others as witnesses. They trained their tongues to lie by means of the Gospel, for they are godless and without reverence. Without shame, they dared to display the foul mire of their words through accusations against your high priesthood. They forgot and put out of their sight all the great and glorious things done for them through your hands. And things that cannot be believed of your holy person they dared to write down and read in the assembly. Even if your fatherhood had been their gatekeeper in one of the villages for sixty-eight years, they would have been obliged to remain faithful in recognition of your labors on their behalf. How much more are they obliged now, since you have borne the burden of the whole East and endured many sufferings because of their oppression! For their sake you drove sleep from your eyes and rest from your body. And now that your limbs have ceased their labor, how greatly they ought to have made a good return to your fatherhood, since you received them like a merciful father. Yet in return for these good things from you, they, like serpents

full of venom, attacked your venerable old age, although even demons, for all their savagery, recoil and turn back at the sight of the glorious crown of your old age. And if they laid hands on your high priesthood, since this was what they were intent upon and prepared to do, why, your holiness, were you striking the Gospel? And a little further on: You became like the prophet Habakkuk, who, because of the injustice he saw, was ready to bring a case against his Creator. And for this reason you received the sentence in your own person, and not, as you led the foolish there to believe, because Papa received punishment for the disgraceful things that were in him. Far be it from us to think as they do. But if, when they spat in Christ’s face and struck him on
his cheeks, and beat him on the head and mocked him, and afterward uprooted altars and killed priests, and trampled on the holy sacrament, which is his

atoning body—and these very things were done not only by enemies, but even more by members of the household, by those who call themselves shepherds, whose fire even now [?] in our churches, and who are not satisfied with our slaughter and destruction—and the orthodox who are with us

received no punishment. Your Holiness, however, did not receive punishment because of those things that were said against you. For it is clear and evident that they are all matters of injustice and oppression, committed in their insolence before the altar

and the Gospel. A terrible reckoning is reserved for them on that terrible day of judgment. But as for Your Holiness having acted insolently toward the Gospel when you were overcome by rage at their oppression, the Lord did not wish to forget your good works and disregard your fine conduct, and reserve this against you for the day of judgment, as with them, so that, just as they are judged for their insolence, you too should be judged with them and like them. Rather, your merciful Lord, whom you served with a pure heart, and who always

accepted the prayers you offered before him over a span of a hundred years and more, showed you favor, pardoned you, and forgave your offenses. Through a slight punishment that he brought upon your holy body, and through a small sentence, passing and temporary, he removed the coming judgment from you. And although we all share deeply in your suffering, we have comfort in this: we have heard that immediately, on the heels of the offense, punishment appeared in your body. God’s testimony about you is trustworthy: you are his faithful and true foster child, and you were brought up in conduct pleasing to God until that lapse. And for that very lapse he struck you as a beloved son with the rod of his discipline. But those who are strangers and not sons were, for this reason, not given discipline as Your Fatherhood was. As for you, because the Lord loved
you, he disciplined you and made you his own. You grieve also over those others, because they are reserved for everlasting torment. As for the suffering concerning the whole flock of your region,

we have learned what confusion, disturbances, and divisions Satan has cast into your region: as though those within had not enough to do in fighting those outside, they also fell upon one another. The conflict within became fiercer than the one outside. And we know that, in the end, the warfare of those outside gained great strength from this warfare among those within, because those apostates and worthless men show them paths and evil ways. And you will have to witness a great persecution that they raise against the church of God in your region. Concerning these things, we have this to say: it would have been better if the great gift of the patriarchate had not been given to the see of Your Holiness. And because no metropolitans had been appointed in the region of the East, all the bishops were subject to the see of Your Holiness. But now, on account of the patriarchate, your honor has been diminished. And it is clear that it was because of pride and not

Compliance with the metropolitans whom you appointed: your honor has been diminished. And we know that the metropolitans, if they had an attitude of submission toward their own patriarchs, would not have allowed disputes to multiply in your region. But it has become clear from the information, and also from the letters of our brother Mar Jacob, that they themselves cause these disputes and make them grow. For the metropolitans do not want the patriarch to be the judge who holds them accountable for their offenses. From time to time they troubled our fathers with complaints against their own patriarchs. And when their accusations were examined and investigated, not only were the patriarchs found innocent of the accusations against them, but the metropolitans and bishops were found guilty. Some of them were deposed and removed from their ranks. Because of the resentment and hatred that had grown among them, they accepted no discipline and made no correction. And now they are striking the church of your region with the lashes of their schisms and with the [?] of their division. We have judged and considered within ourselves that this would help
the church of God in our region and yours: what our earlier fathers approved when they granted the authority

of the patriarchate to your eastern see at the church of Kokhe, so that he might appoint metropolitans where he knows it would be helpful, and have authority over them [also] to appoint them when they are worthy and to depose them for their offenses. Likewise, concerning all the bishops of the East, the patriarch is to hold them accountable and be their judge throughout the whole church of God in the eastern region. He is to exercise authority and govern. We too have agreed to this and approved it: whenever anyone engages in disputes, causes disturbances, and pulls his neck away from submission to the patriarch’s leadership, the patriarch is to depose that person and appoint another in his place. He is to have authority over all appointments, releases, and dismissals
[of judges], corrections, and the establishment of canons, and to increase or reduce churches and monasteries,
and also episcopal sees, even if it is necessary to reduce them for the stability and benefit of other churches and sees
of bishops.
